name: Daily Dispatch
one_line: LinkedIn for people who know they should post and never do. Drop photos in a folder, get one email every morning, press one button.
writeup: Most people know they should post on LinkedIn. Almost nobody does, because it means opening LinkedIn.

Daily Dispatch turns it into one decision a day. You drop photos into a Google Drive folder. Overnight it writes a caption in your voice and lays out a post. At 9 a.m. it lands in your inbox, and you press Approve, Skip or Reject. Nothing goes out without that click.
gaps: Public front page only; sign-in and sign-up pages were not opened. The page's sample stats panel is the site's own mock, not real usage. Inclusion is the owner's call. Logo left out: the only one on file is a purple wordmark with the old name, Postinnator.

name: Page 22
one_line: A crane game for Reneev's Page 22, a 22-storey tower. Stack all 22 real floors and top it out. The building never falls.

facts.label: Role
facts.value: Designed and built it for the launch.

writeup: Page 22 is a residential tower by Reneev, 22 floors. The game lets you build it: a crane swings each floor in, you tap to drop it, and you try to get all 22 up.

Every floor is cut from the real architectural render, so the tower you finish is the actual building. One rule from the start: you never watch the client's building collapse. A bad drop drains a stability meter instead, and the tower just sways.
gaps: Thin. Three phone-shaped frames and one desktop start screen; no frame of the finished tower with the crown. Client work for Reneev, so inclusion is the owner's call.

name: LitPro
one_line: Plan the lights before the truck arrives. Add a photo of the location, place real fixtures, get the numbers.
writeup: On a recce, everyone guesses the truck list. LitPro lets you plan it on a photo of the location instead.

Add the photo and it works out the depth of the room on your own machine. Place real fixtures from a list, and it gives you what a gaffer actually needs: the light level at the subject, each light's ratio to the key in stops, whether a fixture can reach that from where it stands, and the total amps. The picture is nice. The numbers are the product.
gaps: Very thin. One frame of the empty start state; nothing shows a lit location or the numbers. The live page still calls itself Sparks, not LitPro. Inclusion is the owner's call.
